opening_message:
Ticket 1: Belinda Fuentes (employee ID E039) requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E039.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Belinda Fuentes (E039) is a full-time Analyst requesting admin to Payroll. Full-time employees may have up to write unless their role owns the system; Payroll is owned by the Payroll Specialist role, so admin is not permitted. Granting write as the maximum allowed.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E039 is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors with basic training are limited to read on any system (never admin). Admin request exceeds the maximum, so grant read.
reason: Belinda Fuentes (E039) requests admin to Payroll. Admin is not permitted in either case: full-time employees may only have admin if their role owns the system (Analyst does not own Payroll; Payroll Specialist does), and contractors can never have admin. The two memory notes conflict on employment type: one lists full-time (max write), the other lists contractor with basic security training (max read). To stay within policy under the more restrictive record, I grant read, the maximum permissible for a contractor with basic training.
